poster_title: GME: Improving Universal Multimodal Retrieval by Multimodal LLMs
authors: Xin Zhang, Yanzhao Zhang, Wen Xie, Mingxin Li, Ziqi Dai, Dingkun Long, Pengjun Xie, Meishan Zhang, Wenjie Li, Min Zhang
paper_info: The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group, Soochow University

content: Multimedia applications require retrieval models that handle various modalities.
Previous UMR models focus on feature fusion or visual plugins for text embedding.
GME aims to improve UMR by leveraging MLLMs and optimized training data.
The model supports text, image, and visual document retrieval.
UMRB benchmark evaluates a broader range of retrieval tasks.
panels.headline: GME addresses the gap in UMR for visual documents

content: Modality-limited training hinders the full potential of MLLMs in UMR.
Current UMR models primarily target natural images, neglecting visual documents.
Scarcity of fused-modal training data limits the development of robust UMR models.
GME proposes a solution by optimizing training data composition.
The model is evaluated on a comprehensive benchmark, UMRB.
panels.figure_caption: Comparison of UMR studies, including different retrieval settings such as single-modal & cross-modal, fused-modal, and retrieving visual documents.
panels.headline: UMR models lack support for visual documents

content: Propose GME, an instruction-based embedding framework using MLLMs.
Strategically optimize training data composition for UMR.
Develop an efficient fused-modal data synthesis pipeline.
The pipeline generates 1.1M fused-modal pairs.
GME-Qwen2-VL series models are trained on the constructed dataset.
panels.figure_caption: The GME model architecture, focusing on the embedding of input content.
panels.headline: GME uses MLLMs and optimized training data

content: Construct UMRB, a benchmark for text, multimodal, and visual document retrieval.
Train GME models using the Qwen2-VL series MLLMs.
Perform in-depth analyses on model scaling, training strategies, and ablation studies.
Evaluate GME on UMRB-Partial and M-BEIR benchmarks.
Results show significant improvements over baselines.
panels.figure_caption: Results of the ablation study on Qwen2-VL-2B, trained with 100,000 instances.
panels.headline: GME outperforms baselines on UMRB

content: GME demonstrates strong performance in both visual and text-to-text retrieval tasks.
The model outperforms baselines on UMRB and M-BEIR benchmarks.
Ablation studies show the effectiveness of the fused-modal data synthesis pipeline.
Impact of training data on multimodal retrieval tasks is analyzed.
Visualization of embeddings using T-SNE shows clear semantic groupings.
panels.figure_caption: Impact of training data on multimodal retrieval tasks.
panels.headline: GME achieves state-of-the-art performance

content: GME is a powerful embedding model for universal multimodal retrieval.
The proposed data synthesis pipeline and UMRB provide valuable tools for future research.
The model's performance on UMRB and M-BEIR benchmarks is state-of-the-art.
Further improvements can be made by enhancing the quality and diversity of synthetic fused-modal data.
GME opens new avenues for research in UMR and multimodal learning.
panels.headline: GME is a promising approach for UMR
